questions.stem: Why do large multicellular organisms need specialised transport systems, while single-celled organisms do not?

options.text: Large organisms have a small surface area to volume ratio, so diffusion alone is too slow to supply all cells
Large organisms produce more heat, which requires a transport system to cool down
Single-celled organisms use active transport instead of diffusion
Single-celled organisms do not need any substances to survive

questions.explanation: As organisms increase in size, their surface area to volume ratio decreases. This means diffusion alone cannot supply substances quickly enough to all the cells deep inside the body. Specialised transport systems like the circulatory system in animals and xylem/phloem in plants are needed to move substances efficiently.
